title: Hot Deserts and the Sahara
welcome_lead: Cross dunes and gravel plains in the world's largest hot desert.
meta_desc: Geography Adventure: hot deserts, adaptations and the Sahara as a case study.
final_note: You have crossed the Sahara — fragile, fascinating and increasingly stressed by climate change.

walkthroughs.body_html: Most hot deserts lie under the descending limb of Hadley cells around 20-30°N/S, where air sinks and warms, suppressing rainfall. Cold offshore currents (Canary, Benguela, Humboldt) and rain shadow effects intensify aridity. The Sahara experiences extreme diurnal ranges, with summer temperatures above 40 °C and nights sometimes below 0 °C.

Xerophytic plants like acacia and date palm survive through deep roots, succulence and reduced transpiration. Camels, fennec foxes and addax demonstrate physiological and behavioural adaptations. Tuareg, Bedouin and Berber peoples have managed scarce water and pastures through nomadic and oasis-based strategies.

Oil and gas in Algeria and Libya, phosphates in Morocco and emerging solar projects (Noor in Morocco) drive economic interest. Climate change, population growth and overgrazing fuel desertification along the Sahel, where the Great Green Wall aims to restore land across 11 countries.

mcqs.q: Why is the urban heat island effect strongest at night?
options: At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
Urban heat islands only happen in summer.
Concrete and brick released their stored daytime heat slowly into the night air, while rural areas cool rapidly through radiative loss — widening the urban-rural temperature gap after sunset.
Urban heat islands are strongest at midday because cities are sunniest then.

mcqs.q: What happens at a constructive (divergent) plate boundary?
options: At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
At constructive boundaries the plates collide and build mountains.
Plates move apart, magma rises to fill the gap and solidifies, forming new oceanic crust — for example at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
U-shaped valleys form when rivers freeze and expand.

mcqs.q: How do glaciers form U-shaped valleys?
options: Urban heat islands only happen in summer.
Glaciers carve U-shaped valleys from flat land by pushing through.
Glaciers erode existing V-shaped river valleys through plucking (freezing onto rock and pulling pieces away) and abrasion (rock embedded in the ice scraping the valley floor and sides).
U-shaped valleys form when rivers freeze and expand.
